stem: A project installs two dbt Hub packages and one private Git package whose specification uses a Jinja-rendered access token. The team wants to adopt cross-project references, which requires `dependencies.yml`, and must keep the private package installable. Which arrangement of files works?

option_texts.A: Declare the private package in `dependencies.yml` and leave the two hub packages listed in `packages.yml`
option_texts.B: Declare all three packages and the cross-project refs in `dependencies.yml`
option_texts.C: Declare everything in `packages.yml`, which also accepts cross-project refs
option_texts.D: Declare the hub packages and cross-project refs in `dependencies.yml`, keeping the private package in `packages.yml`

drill_answer_short: Split them: dependencies.yml cannot hold a private package, because it does not render Jinja
decision_hinge: Private packages are not supported in dependencies.yml because they intentionally don't support Jinja rendering or conditional configuration.

plausible_options.B: The team wants to adopt cross-project references, which requires `dependencies.yml`

A.signal: one private Git package whose specification uses a Jinja-rendered access token
A.requires_fact: Private packages are not supported in dependencies.yml because they intentionally don't support Jinja rendering or conditional configuration.

C.signal: The team wants to adopt cross-project references, which requires `dependencies.yml`
C.requires_fact: Use dependencies.yml when you need to set up cross-project references between different dbt projects, especially in a dbt Mesh setup.

distractor_traps.A: T8: scope error — it puts exactly the one package that cannot live in dependencies.yml there
distractor_traps.B: T6: treats dependencies.yml as a drop-in rename of packages.yml, which breaks the private package
distractor_traps.C: T3: packages.yml handles package dependencies only — cross-project refs need dependencies.yml

stem: An analyst runs `dbt run --select customers`, then immediately runs `dbt show --select customers`. The previewed rows do not match what a warehouse client returns for the same table, and the team must explain the discrepancy before changing anything. What explains the difference?

option_texts.A: dbt show reads the built table but caps the preview at five rows
option_texts.B: dbt show reads the model's most recent run results artifact rather than the built warehouse table
option_texts.C: dbt show renders the compiled SQL without executing it against the warehouse
option_texts.D: dbt show recompiles and runs the query from source instead of reading the built table

drill_answer_short: dbt show always compiles and runs from source; it never selects the materialized relation
decision_hinge: If previewing a model, dbt will always compile and run the compiled query from source. It will not select from the already-materialized database relation, even if you've just run the model.

plausible_options.A: The previewed rows do not match what a warehouse client returns for the same table

B.requires_fact: If previewing a model, dbt will always compile and run the compiled query from source.

C.signal: the team must explain the discrepancy before changing anything
C.requires_fact: dbt show will run that query against the data warehouse and preview the results in the terminal.

distractor_traps.A: T5: the five-row default is real, but it truncates the preview rather than changing which relation is queried
distractor_traps.B: T1: dbt show does not read run_results.json; there is no such preview path
distractor_traps.C: T3: dbt compile is the command that renders SQL without executing it

stem: A source sets both `loaded_at_field` and `loaded_at_query` on the same table, expecting dbt to fall back from one to the other. The project must parse cleanly before the next deploy. What actually happens?

option_texts.A: Clean parsing, but the `filter` clause is then silently ignored
option_texts.B: A parse warning, after which `loaded_at_query` takes precedence
option_texts.C: Clean parsing, because `loaded_at_field` is used only when adapter metadata is unavailable
option_texts.D: A parse error, because setting both on one resource is not allowed

drill_answer_short: Setting both loaded_at_query and loaded_at_field on one resource is a parse error
decision_hinge: Setting both loaded_at_query and loaded_at_field on the same resource is a parse error.

plausible_options.B: expecting dbt to fall back from one to the other

A.signal: The project must parse cleanly before the next deploy
A.requires_fact: filter adds a WHERE clause to the freshness query to limit data scanned, and does not apply to loaded_at_query.

C.signal: A source sets both `loaded_at_field` and `loaded_at_query` on the same table
C.requires_fact: loaded_at_field is the column dbt queries to determine the most recent loaded timestamp, required when adapter metadata is unavailable.

distractor_traps.A: T2: the filter caveat is about loaded_at_query's scan, not about parsing
distractor_traps.B: T3: dbt defines no precedence between the two — it refuses to parse instead
distractor_traps.C: T5: the metadata-unavailable rule is real but describes when loaded_at_field is needed, not this conflict

stem: A pull request edits only the `tags` value on one model and a column-level `meta` value on another. A Slim CI job selects `state:modified` against the production manifest and builds nothing. The team must explain the empty run. Why was nothing built?

option_texts.A: The comparison manifest was stale, so both edits look unchanged
option_texts.B: Column-level YAML edits never participate in state comparison of any kind
option_texts.C: dbt treats `tags` and `meta` as metadata only, so neither counts
option_texts.D: `persist_docs` is disabled, so YAML-only edits are all ignored

drill_answer_short: tags and meta are metadata-only and deliberately do not trigger state:modified
decision_hinge: dbt treats tags and meta as metadata-only fields, not modifications, at both the resource and column level. Changing a tags or meta value doesn't trigger state:modified, because these fields don't affect how dbt materializes the resource.

plausible_options.D: A Slim CI job selects `state:modified` against the production manifest and builds nothing

A.signal: A pull request edits only the `tags` value on one model
A.requires_fact: state:new means there is no node with the same unique_id in the comparison manifest.

B.requires_fact: description is treated as a modification, but only when persist_docs is enabled, at relation or column level.

distractor_traps.A: T5: a stale manifest is a real failure mode, but it would also hide genuine code changes
distractor_traps.B: T1: column-level edits do participate — a column description counts when persist_docs is on
distractor_traps.D: T3: persist_docs governs descriptions specifically, not every YAML-only edit

stem: A 4 MiB seed file has several rows corrected, with no rename. The CI job runs `--select state:modified --state prod` and the seed is not rebuilt. The team must get the corrected rows into the warehouse on this run. What explains this outcome?

option_texts.A: dbt needs `--full-refresh` before any seed is eligible for state selection
option_texts.B: dbt excludes seeds from state comparison and only ever compares models
option_texts.C: dbt hashes seed contents at every file size, so the hash must be unchanged
option_texts.D: dbt compares only the seed's file path above 1 MiB, so edits are invisible

drill_answer_short: Above 1 MiB dbt falls back to comparing the seed's file path, not its contents
decision_hinge: dbt stores a file hash of seed files that are under 1 MiB in size. If a seed file is over 1 MiB in size, dbt cannot compare its contents and will raise a warning as such. Instead, dbt will use only the seed's file path to detect changes.

plausible_options.C: A 4 MiB seed file has several rows corrected, with no rename

A.signal: The team must get the corrected rows into the warehouse on this run
A.requires_fact: If you provide the --full-refresh flag to dbt run, dbt will treat incremental models as table models.

B.signal: The CI job runs `--select state:modified --state prod` and the seed is not rebuilt
B.requires_fact: If the contents of these seeds is modified, the seed will be included in state:modified.

distractor_traps.A: T2: full-refresh governs rebuild behaviour, not eligibility for state selection
distractor_traps.B: T1: seeds are covered by state comparison; it is the size that changes the method
distractor_traps.C: T8: scope error — content hashing is real, but it only applies below the 1 MiB limit
